description: A gentle 36-week listening and speaking journey. Five playful 5–8 minute sessions each week, with five new words or useful chunks per week. Designed for a complete beginner, with pictures first and optional Arabic script.

words.note: A friendly short greeting. Your family may prefer السلام عليكم (es-salamu ʿlikum).
You may also hear wah or naʿam in different situations.
A calm no is useful too.
A very common Algerian thank-you. When addressing a girl or woman, you may hear ṣaḥḥiti.
Say it with a wave.
Use your own family's name for mum if different.
Use your own family's name for dad if different.
The ending belongs to the whole phrase: my brother.
You may also hear okhti.
Many families use yemma, nana or another affectionate name.
Pause, then add your own name. Wesmi and semmiwni are also heard.
For a boy: طفل (ṭfel).
Rani introduces how or where I am.
For one boy or man: نتا (nta).
You may see ماء or hear l-ma, the water.
Meaning depends on context. Nḥebb ma means I want water.
Addressing one person; use a warm tone and a polite phrase.
Feminine: a big ball is kora kbira.
A common French loan; Arabic spelling varies, including بوبية.
First-person form, used by girls and boys.
With I am: راني فرحانة (rani farḥana). Masculine: farḥan.
Masculine: ʿeyyan. It can also mean unwell in context.
Masculine: djiʿan. You may also hear jiʿana.
Masculine: ʿaṭshan.
Labas? can also be a question: Are you all right?
Masculine form. Feminine: حمرا (ḥamra), as in kora ḥamra.
Masculine form. Feminine: زرقا (zerga). Pronunciation varies: zreq / zreg.
Masculine form. Feminine: خضرا (khaḍra).
Masculine form. Feminine: صفرا (ṣafra).
Masculine form. Feminine: بيضا (bayḍa).
Use for counting. Before a feminine noun, waḥda is used in some patterns.
Feminine: a big house is dar kbira.
A familiar everyday loan word.
My head: راسي (rasi).
My hand: يدي (yeddi).
Context tells whether it means foot or leg. My foot: rejli.
My eye: عيني (ʿini).
My mouth: فمي (fommi).
A common Algerian word; some families use other forms.
Masculine form. Feminine: بنينة (bnina), as in teffaḥa bnina.
Often heard in Algiers. Other families say qett / gaṭṭ; record your family's word.
Used for fish as animals or food.
A widely understood polite form; families may prefer ʿayyshek or rabbi ykhellik.

words.english: Excuse me / sorry (to a girl or woman)
words.french: Excuse-moi (à une fille ou une femme)
words.note: To a boy or man: سمحلي (semḥli).

words.english: Help me (to a girl or woman)
words.french: Aide-moi (à une fille ou une femme)
words.note: To a boy or man: عاونّي (ʿawenni).

words.english: More / add some (to a girl or woman)
words.french: Encore / ajoute (à une fille ou une femme)
words.note: To a boy or man: زيد (zid). Use with an object or a gesture.
A useful way to say you have had enough.
Feminine: كبيرة (kbira).
Feminine: صغيرة (ṣghira).
Feminine: طويلة (ṭwila).
Feminine: قصيرة (qṣira).
Feminine: مليحة (mliḥa).
French loan word; spelling varies.
French loan word.
French loan; families may use it for different knitted tops.
Often used collectively.
French loan word.
You may also hear wra.
Here this means the grass in a garden.
You may also hear shṭa or nnu for rain/weather, depending on family.
Feminine: سخونة (skhouna). Weather: راهو سخون (rahou skhoun).
Feminine: باردة (barda).
Common loan word; also written طوموبيلة.
Often pronounced wesh. Learn your family's vowel.
Dorka, derwek and other regional forms are also heard.
The vowel distinguishes this from byeḍ, white. One egg: بيضة (biḍa).
A common French loan; pronunciation varies.
Used beyond meals too, such as for a new purchase.
Names for dishes vary between households; use your family's bowl word.
You may hear moghorfa; the exact word and size vary by family.
For pretend play or a cool, empty pot with an adult.
First-person present: I get up. The initial n is held a little longer. A common shorter written form is نوض.
Literally: I wash my teeth.
Use with context, such as getting ready for school.
Past tense; same first-person form for girls and boys.
Joins words or ideas; often attached to the following word in writing.
It can have other meanings in different contexts.
You may also hear khater or ḥit.
For example: ki nelʿab, neḍḥak — when I play, I laugh.
Ma…sh makes many verbs negative.

words.english: Say it again (to a girl or woman)
words.french: Répète (à une fille ou une femme)
words.note: To a boy or man: عاود (ʿawed).
A whole useful question; no need to analyse it yet.
Your paternal aunt.
Your maternal aunt.
Many speakers use this form for one person; feminine endings vary by family.
For a masculine noun: هذا (hada). Often spelled هادي.
For a feminine thing: تعجبني (taʿdjebni).
For a feminine thing: ما تعجبنيش (ma taʿdjebnish).
A request for help can come next.
A future pattern: raḥ + action. Rayḥa nrouḥ is another common form for a girl.
A common family expression for a hope or future plan; optional to use.

words.english: Can you hear me? (to a girl or woman)
words.french: Tu m'entends ? (à une fille ou une femme)
words.note: To a boy or man: تسمعني؟ (tesmaʿni?).

words.english: I missed you / I miss you
words.note: Addressing one person. Families differ in final vowel pronunciation.
Choose someone she is comfortable saying this to.
A warm expression of appreciation; literally a wish for health.
Masculine: shaṭer. Celebrate effort, curiosity and trying, not perfect pronunciation.

weeks.title: Hello, little star!
weeks.goal: Greet someone, answer yes or no, and close a tiny conversation.
weeks.familyActivity: Let two toys meet. She can wave, choose yes or no, and say goodbye. A gesture counts as an answer.
weeks.scriptFocus: Pictures first. Arabic can stay hidden; nobody needs to read.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Wave for salam; nod for ih; shake your head for la. Say each once, then let her choose the gesture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add thanks and goodbye with a toy that brings a pretend gift. Swap roles after two turns. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Hide one of the five picture cards. Let her point to or name the missing greeting. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: A toy says hello. Let her answer by voice or a wave, then end the visit. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Use one greeting with a real family member today. Keep it playful and stop after one happy exchange. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: My favourite people
weeks.goal: Recognise five family names and connect them with familiar faces.
weeks.phraseEnglish: Mum, Dad, my sister, my brother.
weeks.phraseFrench: Maman, Papa, ma sœur, mon frère.
weeks.familyActivity: Use photos or draw a pretend family. Relatives who are absent can be represented by a toy; family structures can differ.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice that Arabic lines begin on the right. No letter names yet.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show three photos for mum, dad and brother. Say each name and let her point or pass you the matching photo. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add sister and grandmother. Put the photos in two piles and let her find the one you name. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use the three new family cards with hello and goodbye. Greet each person, then wave goodbye. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: Let her choose a photo and introduce it using just one family word. You model once, then wait. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Make a tiny family picture book with any three people she chooses and label them aloud. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Here I am
weeks.goal: Say who I am and recognise a short introduction.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I am a girl. I am here.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je suis une fille. Je suis ici.
weeks.familyActivity: Play a gentle peekaboo game with a scarf. She can reveal herself and say rani hna, or let a toy do it.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ا in أنا. Simply notice the tall stroke; tracing is optional.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Point to yourself for ana, say your own name after esmi, then introduce ṭefla with a picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add rani hna and nti. Point to yourself and your partner; do not test grammar. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use I, my name and girl alongside mum and dad. Point to the speaker, then let a toy introduce itself. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Listen to the story Here I Am. Pause after each short line so she can point to the speaker. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Record a tiny introduction for yourselves, or say it to a toy: hello, my name is…, I am here. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A little snack
weeks.goal: Ask for a familiar drink or food with a gesture and a short chunk.
weeks.familyActivity: Set up a pretend café with empty cups and pictures of bread and milk. Accept pointing, then model the request warmly.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot م in ما and ماما. Let her find it without naming every letter.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Put water, bread and milk pictures on the table. Name one and let her feed a toy. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add nḥebb and ʿṭini. Offer two choices; she can ask with one word or the whole chunk. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use water, bread and milk with mum and dad. Let her deliver the item you name to the chosen family picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: Practise ʿṭini ma with an empty cup. Switch who asks and who gives; add a warm thank-you. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: At one real snack, pause for a choice. Model her request once and celebrate any attempt. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Let's play!
weeks.goal: Recognise play words and choose a favourite toy.
weeks.familyActivity: Roll a ball, look for a toy and listen to a gentle sound. Follow her choice of play rather than finishing every card.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice that ب has one dot underneath. Find it in نلعب if interested.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show a ball and doll, then act out playing. Say kora, poupiya and nelʿab as you do each. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add nshouf and nesmaʿ. Play I see / I hear with a visible toy and a soft clap. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix ball, doll and I play with water and bread. Sort things a toy can play with and things for a snack. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: Offer the two toys. Model nḥebb nelʿab, then let her choose how to invite you. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Spend two minutes playing her game. Repeat one Darja word naturally a few times. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: How do I feel?
weeks.goal: Name a feeling or need using a girl's speaking form.
weeks.familyActivity: Make faces together. Let her choose her real feeling; there is no correct feeling and she can pass.
weeks.scriptFocus: Look for the round ة ending in فرحانة. It often appears in these feminine words.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Make happy, tired and hungry faces. Let her match a face or toy to the three words. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add thirsty and fine. Pair thirsty with water and hungry with bread from week 4. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use happy, tired and hungry with mum and ball. Show how a toy feels before or after play. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Thirsty Doll together. Ask for a picture answer before inviting speech. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Ask once how she feels. Offer two picture choices, then respond to what she actually needs. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A rainbow hunt
weeks.goal: Hear five colour names and notice the feminine form with a ball.
weeks.familyActivity: Search for coloured objects around the room. Use only safe objects within reach, and let her choose the hunt route.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ر in حمر and خضر. Colour pictures matter more than reading; noticing one familiar shape is enough.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Place red, blue and green objects in front of you. Say one colour and let her touch it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add yellow and white. Sort five toy pieces into colour piles, with no speed race. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Pair red, blue and green with ball and doll. Model the colour ending in kora ḥamra without asking for a grammar rule. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She becomes the colour caller. You deliberately pick the wrong colour once and let her fix it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Find one red thing and one blue thing together. Share the colour in Darja at any time today. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Count my treasures
weeks.goal: Recognise and say the counting sequence from one to five.
weeks.familyActivity: Count large blocks, toy animals or claps. Count objects one at a time; she may count along or simply move them.
weeks.scriptFocus: Try ١ ٢ ٣ beside 1 2 3. These are numeral shapes, not a reading test.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use one, two and three blocks. Touch each block as you count slowly and stop at three. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add four and five. Build two small towers and count them together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Match one, two and three with ball and doll. Count toy pictures or claps slowly. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She tells you how many claps to make, using a word, fingers or a number card. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Count five steps or five toys together once today. Finish with a silly celebration. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Our cosy home
weeks.goal: Find five familiar things at home.
weeks.familyActivity: Give a toy a tour of one room. Name the door, window, chair and table as you pass them together.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot د in دار. Draw the shape in the air if she wants.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use home, door and window pictures. Name one, then point to its real-life match. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add chair and table. Move a toy between them and name the place each time. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit red and one with home, door and window. She can name a picture, spot a colour or count one object. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Ball at Home. Let her point to the chair when she hears it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Let her guide you to one named object in the room and finish by saying rani fi d-dar. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Head to toe
weeks.goal: Recognise five body words through actions.
weeks.familyActivity: Play a slow touch-your-head game. She touches her own body or a doll; adults do not need to touch her.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ع in عين. Listen to an adult first; comfortable attempts are enough.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Point to your own head, hand and foot. She can copy with herself or a doll. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add eye and mouth. Make a funny face, then point to the part you name. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use head, hand and foot with tired and happy. A toy can show a feeling and point to a body part. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: Let her be the caller. You point to the named body part, including one playful mistake. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: At handwashing, say yeddi once together. Connect the word to what you are already doing. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Fruit picnic
weeks.goal: Choose fruit and describe a tasty bite.
weeks.familyActivity: Use fruit pictures or food already suitable for your child. Give a toy a picnic and let her choose what it eats.
weeks.scriptFocus: Find ت in تفّاحة and تمر. Notice the two dots above.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce apple, banana and orange with real fruit or pictures. Let her point before repeating. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add dates and tasty. Use bnin for bread and bnina for an apple; these are models, not grammar drills. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Sort apple, banana and orange with water and milk. Ask for one item and let her pass its picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She orders a fruit using nḥebb plus its name. You offer it and wait for a response. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Choose one fruit at snack time. Ask her opinion and accept any answer, including not liking it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Animal friends
weeks.goal: Identify five animals and follow a tiny picture story.
weeks.familyActivity: Walk a toy animal through a paper garden. She chooses the animal and can copy its movement or sound.
weeks.scriptFocus: Look for ح in حوت. Contrast the written shape with خ only if she is curious.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce cat, dog and bird using pictures and playful movement. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add fish and rabbit. Mix the five cards and ask her to give an animal to a toy. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use cat, dog and bird with red and two. Choose an animal, count two toy animals or add a colour to a drawing. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Bird and the Rabbit. Offer the two animal pictures when asking the story question. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: On a walk or in a picture book, name one animal she notices. Let her lead the looking. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Kind little requests
weeks.goal: Ask for help, more, or a stop with polite words.
weeks.familyActivity: Build a small block tower that needs two people. Practise help me, more and enough; always honour enough.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ي at the end of عاونيني and زيدي. Hear the girl-to-woman forms together.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Model please, sorry and help me with two toys. She can choose the card for what the toy needs. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add more and enough. Give blocks one by one; stop immediately when she says or shows barka. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit water and ball with please, sorry and help me. Make a short request, then swap roles. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She asks an adult or toy for help with a simple task. Use the form for the person she is addressing. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Invite one real request today and respond warmly. Repeat a clearer model without making her redo it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Big and small
weeks.goal: Describe the size of a familiar object.
weeks.phraseEnglish: A big ball, a small ball.
weeks.phraseFrench: Un grand ballon, un petit ballon.
weeks.familyActivity: Compare toy sizes. Use kbir with masculine words and kbira with feminine words in your own models; let her listen.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ة in كبيرة and صغيرة. A matching ending can sound like a little a.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show a big toy, a small toy and a tall block tower. Act out the three descriptions. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add short and good. Compare two towers; use mliḥ to comment on a helpful idea. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Choose big, small and tall with ball and home. Model kora kbira and dar ṣghira with pictures. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She chooses which toy fits in a box. Let a gesture come first, then offer one descriptive word. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Find one big and one small thing together. She can describe them with a word or a two-word chunk. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: My school bag
weeks.goal: Name familiar school things and say I read.
weeks.familyActivity: Pack a pretend schoolbag with a book and pen. Add her own favourite item and say its name in any language.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ك in كتاب and كرطابل. Writing is optional; pointing is plenty.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Name school, schoolbag and book while looking at pictures or real objects. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add pen and I read. Open a picture book and pretend to read together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use school, schoolbag and book with hello and goodbye. A toy arrives at school, greets you and packs its book. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Little Book. She may turn pages, point, or supply the repeated word ktab. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Let her show one thing from her bag and tell you about it with any Darja word she remembers. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Getting dressed
weeks.goal: Name everyday clothes and use I wear.
weeks.familyActivity: Dress a doll or choose clothes from a basket. Let her decide what the doll wears and explain with one word.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot س in سروال and ص in صباط. The different sounds take time; no perfect imitation needed.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce trousers, top and shoes by holding them up or using pictures. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add dress and I wear. Dress a toy and model nelbes plus the clothing word. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Match trousers, top and shoes with red and blue. Describe a picture while she points to the colour. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She chooses an outfit for a toy and tells you one thing it wears. Silly choices are welcome. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Name one item while getting dressed. She can finish the phrase nelbes… if she wants. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Things I can do
weeks.goal: Understand and use five familiar action words.
weeks.familyActivity: Take turns miming everyday actions. A correct gesture counts; saying the word is an invitation.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ن at the start of نكتب and نرسم. In these examples it helps say I do something.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Mime I eat, I drink and I draw. She guesses by pointing to the matching picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add I write and I sleep. Act out a silly day with the five actions. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix I eat, I drink and I draw with book and water. Choose the object that fits, or mime the action. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She picks two actions for you to mime, then tries saying her own two-action sentence. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: During a familiar activity, describe your own action in Darja and invite her to join once. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Where is my ball?
weeks.goal: Ask where and understand four position words.
weeks.phraseEnglish: The ball is under the chair.
weeks.phraseFrench: Le ballon est sous la chaise.
weeks.familyActivity: Hide a ball in an easy, visible place. Ask win? and let her move the ball to give the answer.
weeks.scriptFocus: Find the familiar ك in الكرة and الكرسي. Read the whole phrase only if she wants.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce where, on and under using a toy and a chair. Make the contrast obvious. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add in front of and behind. Move a toy around a box while saying each place. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use where, on and under with ball and chair. Let her move the ball while you describe its place. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Hiding Ball. Pause for a point or a guess before showing the next line. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Let her hide a toy in plain sight and become your guide. Celebrate finding it together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A garden adventure
weeks.goal: Notice and name five things in a garden.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I see a flower in the garden.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je vois une fleur dans le jardin.
weeks.familyActivity: Look at a garden, balcony plant or picture. Let her choose a favourite detail to draw and label aloud.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ج in شجرة and جنينة. It is often pronounced dj in Algiers speech.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show tree, flower and grass pictures. Let her match each to a drawing or nearby plant. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add soil and garden. Build a paper garden with the five picture cards. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit green and small with tree, flower and grass. Describe one garden picture together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She gives a toy a garden tour using nshouf plus one plant word. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Find one living plant together and tell a family member one Darja word about it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Sun, rain and wind
weeks.goal: Recognise simple weather words and connect them to the day.
weeks.familyActivity: Make a paper weather wheel. She points to today's weather and chooses a matching picture or outfit.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ش in شمس and ر in ريح. Seeing a familiar shape is enough.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce sun, rain and wind with gestures and pictures; make a soft wind sound. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add hot and cold. Match clothing pictures to pretend weather, then say the adjective. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix sun, rain and wind with water and top. Ask what a toy might need in the weather picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She chooses pretend weather for a toy's outing and tells you one word about it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Look out of the window together. Say one true weather word and let her agree or correct you. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A trip together
weeks.goal: Talk about walking, going, coming and two places or objects outside.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I go to the shop with Dad.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je vais au magasin avec Papa.
weeks.familyActivity: Draw a route from home to a pretend shop. Move a toy along it, on foot or in a car; use any familiar caregiver.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot ح in حانوت and روح. Let the adult model the breathy sound gently.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Act out I walk, I go and I come with a toy. She moves it as she listens. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add car and shop. Choose how the toy travels to the pretend shop. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit home and goodbye with I walk, I go and I come. Move a toy away from home and back again. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read A Walk to the Shop. Put down the home, shop and apple pictures as the story unfolds. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: On a normal outing, name where you are going. She can add nrouḥ or wave besslama. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Little questions
weeks.goal: Recognise five question words and enjoy asking one.
weeks.familyActivity: Put familiar photos and objects in a mystery bag. Ask who for a person and what for a thing, then switch roles.
weeks.scriptFocus: Spot و in واش and وقتاش. Questions can be understood by voice before print.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce what, who and why with a toy, a family photo and a simple pretend problem. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add how and when. Show how to build a tower and point to a time picture for when. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use what, who and why with mum and ball. Try who for the family picture and what for the toy; offer a simple picture-supported reason for why. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She chooses a question card for you to answer. Give a short answer she can understand with a picture. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Invite her to ask one Darja question about anything at home. It is fine to answer partly in English or French. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Today and tomorrow
weeks.goal: Connect five time words to familiar routines.
weeks.phraseEnglish: Today I play. Tomorrow I read.
weeks.phraseFrench: Aujourd'hui je joue. Demain je lis.
weeks.familyActivity: Draw three boxes for yesterday, today and tomorrow. Place one routine picture in each; keep plans flexible.
weeks.scriptFocus: Look at اليوم as a whole shape. Do not ask her to sound out every letter.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use yesterday, today and tomorrow cards beside pictures of familiar activities. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add now and later. Move a toy between a now mat and a later mat as you describe a plan. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use today, tomorrow and yesterday with I play and I read. Match one familiar action to a time. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She chooses one thing for now and one for later, saying a word or placing the cards. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: At the end of the day, share one thing from today. Ask what she would enjoy tomorrow. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Ten little treasures
weeks.goal: Count from six to ten and combine the two counting sets.
weeks.familyActivity: Lay out ten large objects in two groups of five. Count slowly together and let her move each one.
weeks.scriptFocus: Explore ٦ ٧ ٨ ٩ ١٠ beside 6–10. Use the shapes as a matching game.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Count an existing row of five, then add six, seven and eight one at a time. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add nine and ten. Fill two rows of five; stop to notice when both rows are full. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix six, seven and eight with two and five. Match each number to a row of objects or fingers. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read Ten Treasures. Let her check the collection by counting real objects or the pictures. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Count something useful together, such as ten blocks to put away. Stop if it becomes tiring. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Breakfast together
weeks.goal: Name breakfast foods and use a warm meal expression.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je veux du pain et du fromage.
weeks.familyActivity: Make a pretend breakfast menu from pictures. She orders, serves and says thanks; include only foods your household uses.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ز in زيت and زبدة. These two food words begin with the same letter.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Name eggs, cheese and oil using pictures. Let her choose what belongs on a pretend table. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add butter and beṣ-ṣaḥḥa. Practise the expression while serving a toy. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Combine eggs, cheese and oil with bread and milk. Make a pretend breakfast with two choices. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She orders two foods using nḥebb and w. You repeat the order and she checks it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: At breakfast, name one food and use beṣ-ṣaḥḥa naturally. A smile is a response. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Little kitchen helper
weeks.goal: Recognise five kitchen items and follow a simple request.
weeks.phraseFrench: Donne-moi un verre, s'il te plaît.
weeks.familyActivity: Set a toy table with unbreakable items. Use only cool, empty cookware and stay with her; the game is naming and helping.
weeks.scriptFocus: Find ك in كاس. Compare its shape with the ك in كتاب.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show bowl, spoon and glass pictures or child-safe items. Ask her to pass one. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add plate and pot using toys or cool objects. Sort items for serving and cooking. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit please and give me with bowl, spoon and glass. Take turns requesting and serving. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She asks you for one item, then checks that you chose correctly. Make one funny mistake. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Let her choose one small table-setting job and name the item she carries. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: My morning
weeks.goal: Describe a few steps of a familiar morning routine.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I wash my hands and brush my teeth.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je me lave les mains et je me brosse les dents.
weeks.familyActivity: Draw three morning pictures together. She arranges them in her own order and tells a toy what she does.
weeks.scriptFocus: Find غ in نغسل. Let her hear the voiced sound; it need not be mastered today.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Mime getting up, washing hands and brushing teeth. Let her order those three cards. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add combing hair and getting ready. Put the cards in the order that suits her morning. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix getting up, washing hands and brushing teeth with today and later. Choose one action for now and one for later. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read Lina's Morning. She can act out the steps instead of repeating the lines. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: During one real morning step, say the matching chunk together. One useful phrase is enough. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: I did it!
weeks.goal: Use five first-person past forms to talk about a little event.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I went to the garden and played.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je suis allée au jardin et j'ai joué.
weeks.familyActivity: Make a two-picture memory of something she enjoyed. Model one past-tense phrase and invite her version.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ت at the end of رحت and شفت. These words tell what I did.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Show pictures for I went, I saw and I found. Move a toy through the mini adventure. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add I played and I laughed. Act first, then describe what you just did. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Revisit garden and ball with I went, I saw and I found. Let her choose a sentence for a toy adventure. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She tells a two-part toy adventure using pictures and one or two past words. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Ask about one enjoyable moment today. Offer shoft or lʿabt if she wants a starting word. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Join my ideas
weeks.goal: Link familiar words and thoughts with a few useful connectors.
weeks.familyActivity: Build a silly scene with two toys and one object. Join words with and or with; longer sentences are optional.
weeks.scriptFocus: See و joined to a following word. Listen for the short w sound between ideas.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use and, but and because with picture pairs. Keep the adult's example short and concrete. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add with and when. Put two toys together for with and act an action for when. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use and, but and because with I play and I draw. Model one short idea, then let her choose the action pictures. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She tells you who a toy plays with. Invite one extra detail only if she wants to continue. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: At playtime, say one true sentence with mʿa. Invite a family member to join the same sentence. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Help me understand
weeks.goal: Ask for repetition or a slower voice without embarrassment.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I didn't understand. Say it again slowly.
weeks.phraseFrench: Je n'ai pas compris. Répète doucement.
weeks.familyActivity: Let a toy mumble a silly message. She can ask again or ask what it means; the adult always responds kindly.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice ما…ش around فهمت. Hear the whole negative chunk without a grammar test.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce understood, didn't understand and say it again. You model a confused toy and help it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add slowly and what does it mean? Try one deliberately quick phrase, then slow down when asked. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Combine please and help me with understood, did not understand and say it again. Choose what the toy needs. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Patient Friend. Make the listener's question the most important line. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Use a repair phrase during a real conversation today. Praise asking for help, not pretending to understand. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: More people I love
weeks.goal: Name relatives and friends while sharing a simple family picture.
weeks.phraseEnglish: This is my aunt, my mother's sister.
weeks.phraseFrench: Voici ma tante, la sœur de maman.
weeks.familyActivity: Use real photos, drawings or invented characters. Explain the two aunt words through a simple family tree.
weeks.scriptFocus: Compare خ in خالتي with ح from earlier. One has a dot above.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce grandfather, father's sister and mother's sister with a drawing that shows the connection. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add a boy friend and girl friend. Let her draw or choose the people she wants to include. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Mix grandfather and the two aunt cards with mum and dad. Put them on a paper family map. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She introduces two chosen people using a word or hadi plus a name. No family details need to be shared outside the home. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Ask a relative for the affectionate name they use at home, then add that version to your family's practice. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Mine and yours
weeks.goal: Say what I have and describe simple ownership.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I have a ball. The ball is mine.
weeks.phraseFrench: J'ai un ballon. Le ballon est à moi.
weeks.familyActivity: Give each toy one object. Ask who has what, then practise borrowing and returning with a warm thank-you.
weeks.scriptFocus: Recognise عندي as a whole word and notice ع again. Writing remains optional.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use I have, I don't have and mine with two toys and two objects. Let her check the statements. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add yours and this feminine form. Hold up the ball and model hadi kora. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use I have, I do not have and mine with book and ball. Share the objects between two toys and describe what changes. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She tells you one thing she has and one thing a toy has. A short phrase is enough. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: During tidying, ask which item belongs to whom. Model mine and yours without turning it into a test. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: My choices matter
weeks.goal: Express a preference, ability or need for help.
weeks.familyActivity: Offer two play choices. Honour her choice or her no, then model a short Darja response that fits it.
weeks.scriptFocus: Find ق in نقدر. Some families pronounce this sound g; family pronunciation is welcome.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce I like it, I don't like it and I can using two toys and a familiar activity. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add I can't and I choose. Make a toy need help, then let her choose who can help it. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Pair I like it, I do not like it and I can with I draw and I play. Ask which idea is true for her today. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read The Picture I Choose. Let her make a different choice from the character. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Offer a real small choice today and wait for her answer. Help her express it with any familiar word. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A plan for tomorrow
weeks.goal: Share a small future plan and understand waiting or meeting.
weeks.familyActivity: Make a pretend plan with a toy: when, where, and one action. Real plans can change; describe them as hopes.
weeks.scriptFocus: Notice راح before نروح and نلعب. It helps these chunks talk about the future.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Use I will go, I will play and I wait with a toy and a tomorrow card. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add we meet and in sha Allah. Explain that the last expression is a family's way to express a hope, and is optional. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Combine tomorrow and garden with I will go, I will play and I wait. Choose one pretend plan. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She tells a toy one thing she would like to do tomorrow. Offer a picture prompt and wait. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Share one small plan for tomorrow. Let her choose the action word and add her own idea. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: A call full of love
weeks.goal: Handle a short family call and express connection.
weeks.phraseEnglish: Hello! I can hear you. I miss you.
weeks.phraseFrench: Allô ! Je t'entends. Tu me manques.
weeks.familyActivity: Use two pretend phones first. If she wants, practise on a real call with a trusted relative; she can stop at any time.
weeks.scriptFocus: Recognise نحبّك as a familiar whole chunk. The mark over ب tells us to hold it a little longer.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce phone hello, can you hear me and I hear you. Use a pretend call with clear turn-taking. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add I miss you and I love you. Let her choose a comfortable expression, or simply wave. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use goodbye and fine with phone hello, can you hear me and I hear you. Make a tiny call together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: My little voice
sessions.instructions: She leads a pretend call: hello, one message, goodbye. You wait while she decides what to say. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Invite a brief call or an unsent practice recording for a chosen relative. Keep sharing under adult control. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

weeks.title: Our Darja celebration
weeks.goal: Show a few things I can say and feel proud of learning together.
weeks.phraseEnglish: I am learning Darja little by little.
weeks.phraseFrench: J'apprends la darja petit à petit.
weeks.familyActivity: Let her choose favourite words, a story and a game for a family celebration. Revisit favourite weeks any time; finishing is not a fluency test.
weeks.scriptFocus: Choose one favourite Arabic word to copy, decorate or simply recognise. There is no required reading milestone.

sessions.title: Listen & discover
sessions.instructions: Introduce I learn, I speak Darja and little by little. Talk about an attempt she is proud of. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Play with words
sessions.instructions: Add well done and capable. Let two toys encourage each other with warm voices. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Remember & mix
sessions.instructions: Use I learn, I speak Darja and little by little with hello and I love you. Let her build her own tiny message. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Story time
sessions.instructions: Read Little by Little. Ask which moment reminds her of something she can do now. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

sessions.title: Together at home
sessions.instructions: Make a tiny show-and-tell: a greeting, a choice and a favourite sentence. End by choosing the next game together. Keep this visit to 5–8 minutes; stop sooner if she is ready.

stories.title: Here I Am
stories.question: Who says "I am here"?
stories.answer: Lina says it. You can say it about yourself too.

stories.title: The Thirsty Doll

lines.english: Lina: Here is some water for you.
lines.french: Lina : Voilà de l'eau pour toi.

stories.question: What does the doll ask for?

stories.title: The Ball at Home

lines.french: Lina : Je suis à la maison.

lines.english: This is a door. This is a window.
lines.french: Voici une porte. Voici une fenêtre.

lines.english: This is a chair. This is a table.
lines.french: Voici une chaise. Voici une table.

stories.question: What does Lina want to do when she finds the ball?

stories.title: The Bird and the Rabbit
stories.question: Which two animals does Lina see?
stories.answer: She sees a bird and a rabbit.

stories.title: The Little Book

lines.english: There is a bird and a rabbit in it.
lines.french: Il y a un oiseau et un lapin dedans.
Lina : Ma sœur, aide-moi s'il te plaît.

lines.english: My sister: Yes! We will read together.
lines.french: Ma sœur : Oui ! On va lire ensemble.

stories.question: What does Lina ask her sister to help with?
stories.answer: She asks for help reading the book.

stories.title: The Hiding Ball

lines.english: The ball is under the chair!
lines.french: Le ballon est sous la chaise !

stories.question: Where is the ball hiding?
stories.answer: The ball is under the chair.

stories.title: A Walk to the Shop

lines.english: Lina: I go to the shop with Dad.
lines.french: Lina : Je vais au magasin avec Papa.

lines.english: I walk and I see a tree.
lines.french: Je marche et je vois un arbre.

lines.arabic: لينا: سلام! عطيني تفّاحة، من فضلك.
lines.transliteration: Lina: salam! ʿṭini teffaḥa, men faḍlek.
lines.english: Lina: Hello! Give me an apple, please.
lines.french: Lina : Bonjour ! Donne-moi une pomme, s'il te plaît.

lines.english: Dad: This is a red apple.

stories.question: What does Lina ask for at the shop?

stories.title: Ten Treasures

lines.arabic: لينا: واحد، زوج، ثلاثة، ربعة، خمسة.
lines.transliteration: Lina: waḥed, zoudj, tlata, rebʿa, khemsa.
lines.english: Lina: One, two, three, four, five.
lines.french: Lina : Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq.

stories.question: How many treasures does Lina have at the end?

stories.title: Lina's Morning

lines.english: I get dressed and get ready.
lines.french: Je m'habille et je me prépare.

stories.question: What does Lina do before she gets ready?
stories.answer: She washes her hands, brushes her teeth and combs her hair.

stories.title: The Patient Friend

lines.english: My friend is talking to me.
Lina: Say it again slowly, please.
lines.french: Lina : Répète doucement, s'il te plaît.

lines.english: My friend: I am going to the garden.
lines.french: Mon amie : Je vais au jardin.

stories.question: What helps Lina understand her friend?
stories.answer: Her friend says it again slowly.

stories.title: The Picture I Choose

lines.english: I have a book and a pen.
lines.french: J'ai un livre et un stylo.

lines.english: Shall I draw a bird or a flower?
lines.french: Je dessine un oiseau ou une fleur ?

stories.question: What does Lina decide to draw?
stories.answer: She chooses to draw a flower.

stories.title: Little by Little

lines.transliteration: Lina: lyoum lʿabt w rsemt werda.
lines.english: Lina: Today I played and drew a flower.
lines.french: Lina : Aujourd'hui, j'ai joué et dessiné une fleur.

lines.english: Lina: I am learning Darja little by little.
lines.french: Lina : J'apprends la darja petit à petit.

stories.question: How is Lina learning Darja?
stories.answer: Little by little, by speaking with her family.

pronunciationTips.explanation: A breathier h than in English. Listen to your family and imitate gently; never force your throat. Ordinary h and ḥ are shown differently here.
A sound English and French do not have. Let a familiar Darja speaker model it, then try a comfortable approximation. Hearing it comes before producing it.
A soft rough sound like the ch in Scottish loch or German Bach. It is one sound, not k followed by h.
A voiced sound somewhat like a French r. Listen to the beginning of ghe in neghsel; it is different from kh.
A k-like sound made farther back in the mouth. Many Algerian families use g in some words. Follow the voice you want to learn from, without treating another regional form as wrong.
Like sh in English shoe or ch in French chat. Both letters together represent one sound.
Like j in English jam or dj in French djinn. This is common in Algiers; other Algerian varieties can sound different.
A fuller, darker s. Start by listening to the difference; an ordinary s is a useful first attempt.
A fuller, darker t. The dot is a reminder for adults, not something a child has to memorise.
Hold the sound a little longer in words such as ṣaḥḥit. No need to count beats; echo a warm, natural model.
Darja vowels can be very short. Our Latin spelling is a friendly reading aid, not formal IPA or one official Algerian spelling. A family recording is the best guide.

parentGuidance: Start at a complete beginner level. Use the learner's real interests and give them control of the game. Pointing, acting and choosing are real participation.

Offer one 5–8 minute session at a time, usually five short visits a week. Session 1 introduces three cards; session 2 adds two. The other visits reuse and combine them. A week can take longer than seven days.
Listen first, then invite a response. Say or play a word, show a picture or real object, wait, and accept a gesture. Speaking is an invitation; a quiet child may still understand a lot.

Use a trusted Central Algerian / Algiers speaker or your own family recordings as the pronunciation model. A device Arabic voice is an approximate helper: it may read Darja like Standard Arabic and is not an authentic Darja teacher.
Arabic, Latin pronunciation, English and French support the adult. Keep the script and pronunciation guide hidden when they distract from listening. Do not ask her to read in order to take part.

Our examples use feminine forms when the girl describes herself. Some requests also address a girl or woman; card notes give the masculine counterpart. I-action forms such as nelʿab are the same for a girl and a boy.

Darja has regional and family variation and no single everyday spelling. This course aims at Central Algerian speech without claiming one universal standard. Welcome the words used by your own family and record them when possible.

The 12 original mini stories recycle familiar language and include a few supported stretch phrases. Read them with pictures and translations; those extra phrases are listening exposure, not new memorisation requirements.
Ask the story question after enjoying the story. An answer in English or French, a point, or an acted response is useful. Show the answer together rather than scoring pronunciation.

Revisit yesterday, last week and a favourite older week. Remembered words need fewer visits; uncertain words need more friendly encounters. Completing a session records participation, not a claim of fluent speech.

Follow the six stages flexibly. Weeks 1–6 connect words with actions; 7–12 grow listening; 13–18 combine small phrases; 19–24 explore questions and time; 25–30 tell and repair; 31–36 connect with family.

Optional script noticing is gradual: familiar shapes first, then recurring endings and small word patterns. Tracing can be in the air or on paper. This is not a full Arabic literacy or tajweed course.
Use real routines: a snack, getting dressed, a garden walk, a family photo, an ordinary call. Two warm exchanges during the day can matter more than finishing extra screens.
Keep play safe and ordinary: child-safe props, cool empty cookware, food already suitable for her, and an adult for outings. Respect no, enough, and her choice about recording or talking to someone.

This is an authored starter curriculum with selected reference checks, not a native-speaker-certified language course. Before relying on a phrase as your household standard, ask a fluent family member to listen and record the version you use.
Celebrate trying, curiosity and asking for help. There is no need to rush, keep a perfect streak, imitate an accent perfectly, or finish the year on a fixed date.
